slot.brief: Give four carbanions (methyl vs substituted/hybridised variations, e.g. sp3 vs sp2 vs sp C−) and ask to rank their stability.

stem: The increasing order of stability of the following carbanions is: (I) benzyl, (II) allyl, (III) methyl, (IV) tert-butyl.

verdicts.working: Alkyl substitution destabilizes carbanions, so tert-butyl is less stable than methyl. Resonance stabilizes allyl and benzyl carbanions; benzyl is more stabilized than allyl. Thus IV < III < II < I.

working:
Resonance stabilization: benzyl $> $ allyl.
Alkyl carbanions: methyl $> $ tert-butyl (alkyl groups destabilize negative charge).
Thus, increasing stability: IV $< $ III $< $ II $< $ I.

Independent check: Alkyl substitution destabilizes carbanions, so tert-butyl is less stable than methyl. Resonance stabilizes allyl and benzyl carbanions; benzyl is more stabilized than allyl. Thus IV < III < II < I.
solution:
Alkyl groups destabilize carbanions, so methyl is more stable than tert-butyl. Resonance stabilizes allyl and benzyl carbanions, with greater stabilization for benzyl.
Thus, the increasing order of stability is $\text{IV} < \text{III} < \text{II} < \text{I}$.
